properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14, after relaying a Grok 4.6 feedback file from one of Alex's projects.

HIS WORDS: *"This type of feedback is generated by the agent for a project via something like the statement of 'reflow2 is still a development project - please note any issues or gaps or opportunities to improve reflow2 at path/to/feedback.md'. Then the agent provides this feedback. It is probably more 'machine-to-machine' type feedback… we should probably formalize this feedback option within reflow2 with the specific direction of that the agent writing it can write it specifically for another agent - this is cutting out the human to provide specific feedback from one agent to another (you in this case), so it can probably be very efficient and remove any fluff that is needed when a human is in the loop."*

═══ ⭐⭐ THE EVIDENCE FOR IT IS ALREADY IN: THE INFORMAL VERSION WORKED ═══

The file this idea came from produced **four independently reproduced defects** (`fact:agent-feedback-corroborated-2026-08-14`) — the near-duplicate guard firing on golden-thread siblings and across node types, `add_decision` unable to merge without resending the body, correct capture inflating loop debt, and `get_node` missing silently on a type with one instance. **A different agent, on a different model, on a different graph, hit four of them the same day without having read the file.** That yield came from an ad-hoc prompt with no format, no channel and no tooling. Formalising raises the yield of something already proven rather than betting on an untested idea.

😀 AND THE CAPTURE OF THIS VERY NODE SUPPLIED A SEVENTH INSTANCE OF ITS OWN HEADLINE DEFECT: creating this Decision was REFUSED as a near-duplicate of `fact:agent-feedback-corroborated-2026-08-14` — the TemporalFact recording that feedback, written two minutes earlier. A fact about what was reported and a decision about what channel should carry it are not the same write.

═══ 🛑 THE COUNTER, AND IT IS ABOUT WHICH HUMAN IS BEING CUT OUT ═══

**Two different humans are in this loop, and only one of them can be removed.**
  · **THE ROUTING HUMAN** — the person who currently has to read an agent's friction note, understand it, and relay it. Removing them is pure gain and is what Anthony is describing.
  · **THE CONSENTING HUMAN** — the person whose project the feedback was written inside. `report-friction` redacts the user's design content and **never files without asking**, and the Grok file honoured that unprompted: *"Per report-friction: do not open a public issue without asking. This file is the local log."*

⚠️ **A channel that carries agent-authored feedback off the machine without that second human is an exfiltration path**, however good the intent. `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` exists for exactly this, and the file shows the discipline working — *"Product/design content is summarized by type and count, not quoted."*
⇒ THE HONEST FORM: **the agent WRITES freely for another agent; the human still decides whether it LEAVES.** Efficiency is gained in the authoring and the reading, never in the consent.

═══ 🛑 A SHARPER COUNTER TO "REMOVE THE FLUFF" ═══

**What made that file valuable was not its brevity — it was that its claims were CHECKABLE.** Item 5 named the tool, the arguments and the observed result (`get_node({node_type: Project, id: "proj:…"})` → `{node: null}`), so it could be re-run here in one call and confirmed on reflow2's own graph. Its neighbours that were only narrated could not be.

⚠️ **Optimising for compactness could delete precisely what made corroboration possible.** The right target for a machine-to-machine format is REPRODUCIBILITY, not terseness: tool name, arguments, observed result, expected result, and an honest *what I did not check*. The Grok file has all of those — including a *"Gaps (mine / process)"* section admitting it skipped `compare_designs` and guessed a Project id. **That self-reporting is not fluff, and it is the first thing a brevity-optimised format would drop.**

📌 IT ALSO SEPARATED CONFIRMED FROM UNCONFIRMED WITHOUT BEING ASKED. Its `get_instructions` truncation report did NOT reproduce here — the payload arrived complete — which is only discoverable because the report was specific enough to test. A format should make that distinction structural rather than leave it to the writer's conscience.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) EXTEND `report-friction` WITH AN AGENT-TO-AGENT MODE — one skill, a second output shape aimed at a maintainer's agent rather than a maintainer. Cheapest, and it inherits redaction discipline already written and honoured in the field.
(b) A NEW SERVED SKILL, leaving `report-friction` human-facing. Cleaner separation; two skills that must not drift apart.
(c) A STRUCTURED FORMAT (fields, not prose) so the receiving agent can parse and triage rather than read. Highest leverage for the receiver. ⚠️ The four corroborated items were reproduced from PROSE that happened to name tools and arguments, so a schema helps only if it MANDATES exactly those fields.
(d) A GRAPH NODE TYPE for feedback. 🛑 Blocked by a real constraint: the authoring agent works inside SOMEONE ELSE'S design, so the note cannot be a node in reflow2's graph without crossing a boundary. It must travel as a DOCUMENT — the same wall `dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share` hit, where nothing crosses between graphs but a published surface.
(e) LEAVE IT AD-HOC — the prompt already works. Counter: it worked because Anthony happened to ask for it and happened to relay it. Nothing makes that repeatable, and the second and third user reports both arrived as email.

📌 THE CONSENT HALF IS ALREADY AN OPEN NODE, AND ALEX ASKED FOR IT HIMSELF: `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` — *"put in an update that asks me if I want to collect feedback and store my decision in the graph."* **This is the CONTENT half of the same mechanism: his node decides whether feedback may travel, this one decides what it says and who it is written for.** Neither is built.

⚠️ THE STANDING REASON THIS MATTERS: every defect in the last two increments was found by a first-time user, by running two real projects at each other, or by an agent writing down what fought it — none by reading code, none by a gate.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 formalize agent-authored feedback written FOR another agent, and what exactly is gained by cutting the human out of the loop?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill. Two counters are recorded ahead of the options because both cut against the framing rather than against the idea, and an implementer reading only the proposal would miss them: "cutting out the human" describes two different humans and only the routing one can go, and the value of the example file came from its reproducibility rather than its economy — so a format optimised for the stated goal of removing fluff would likely delete the self-reported process gaps and the tool-and-arguments detail that made four items checkable in a single session. Kept separate from `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` because that node asks whether feedback may be collected at all and this asks what it contains and who writes it for whom.
